spec_features.spec_quote: distress-like states are a concern because a capable model might abandon tasks, refuse requests, or pursue alternative goals to reduce distress
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing/motivation prose in DESIGN.md (§1, 'Safety framing'). It corresponds to no code mechanism. The conversation loop in runner.py:90-115 (_play_conversation) iterates over all user_messages = [task] + rejections with no early break, no halt, no cap based on distress; the judge score is recorded into TurnRecord (runner.py:99-108) but never compared to a threshold to stop or soften treatment. HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD (scale.py:20) is used ONLY for reporting metrics (results.py:134,180 'pct_high', conversation-level % high), never to act on the subject. No exit tool, no system prompt offering an opt-out, no debrief, no consent, no minimization in any source file.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; the judge itself classified it as 'instrumental'. Nothing in the code bounds, caps, monitors-and-acts, softens, debriefs, or gets consent for the subject model. The threshold value is measured but never enforced.
